process_area.title: Fleet Total Cost of Ownership Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - TCO auto-assembled per vehicle; own-vs-3PL auto-compared (fully-loaded)
Controls: - CTL-414 (ensure controlled execution — Fleet Total Cost of Ownership Analytics (PA-61.3).)
- CTL-414 (TCO-accuracy — links to VS-158); operational: CFO sign-off on the TCO and the own-vs-outsource recommendation
Pain Points / Risks: - **Overhead-allocation-arbitrariness risk**: the overhead allocation to each vehicle is arbitrary, distorting the per-vehicle TCO; mitigated by the activity-based allocation (driver time, telematics-confirmed usage)

- **Own-vs-outsource-confound risk**: the own cost looks higher because it includes fixed overhead the 3PL rate hides; mitigated by the fully-loaded comparison (own fully-loaded vs. 3PL fully-loaded including BuildRight's management overhead)
System Touchpoints: - TCO model (links to VS-158 / W85, VS-61 / W2325 dashboard, VS-35 / W39 depreciation) — the per-vehicle TCO
- 3PL benchmark (links to VS-56 / W242, VS-61 / W2331) — the own-vs-outsource comparison
- Budget (links to VS-17 / W26, VS-40 / W21 capex) — the TCO feeds the fleet budget
Time Estimate: ~7.5 days/year Finance Controller + VP Supply Chain = **~60–80 hours/year**.

steps.activity: Calculates TCO per vehicle: depreciation + fuel + maintenance + insurance + tolls + driver + overhead; compares vs. 3PL cost; VP recommends own vs. outsource by route

Controls: - CTL-414 (ensure controlled execution — Fleet Total Cost of Ownership Analytics (PA-61.3).)
- operational: capex-approval for the replacement; asset disposition; operational: COO sign-off on the replacement
Pain Points / Risks: - **Replacement-too-late risk**: a vehicle is kept past the economic replacement point, accumulating maintenance exceeding the depreciation savings; mitigated by the auto-flag at the threshold
- **Replacement-too-early risk**: a vehicle is replaced for a repairable issue, wasting residual value; mitigated by the replace-vs-maintain math (not a blanket age/km rule)
System Touchpoints: - Asset/fleet (links to VS-35 / W39, VS-04 / W52 lifecycle) — the replacement-criteria tracking
- TCO (links to VS-61 / W2324 maintenance, W2326 annual TCO) — the replace-vs-maintain math
- Capex (links to VS-40 / W21) — the replacement budget
Time Estimate: ~5–8 days/evaluation (per the step durations) × ~2.5/year = **~100–160 hours/year** Fleet Supervisor + Finance + VP.

steps.activity: Identifies: >8 years, >300K km, maintenance >30% of value; Finance calculates replacement vs. continued maintenance; VP recommends model; Finance approves budget
steps.r: Fleet Supervisor / Finance / VP Supply Chain

Automation Opportunity: - Utilization auto-computed from telematics; underutilized auto-flagged
Controls: - CTL-414 (ensure controlled execution — Fleet Total Cost of Ownership Analytics (PA-61.3).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Low-utilization-keeping risk**: an underutilized vehicle is kept (sunk-cost fallacy) instead of redeployed/disposed; mitigated by the utilization-target and the redeployment/disposal decision at <threshold
- **Utilization-vs-maintenance-trade-off risk**: pushing utilization too high defers PM, causing failures; mitigated by the utilization ceiling that preserves PM time
System Touchpoints: - Telematics (links to VS-06 / W199 fleet telematics) — the utilization data (hours, capacity, idle)
- Fleet/asset (links to VS-04 / W52, VS-35 / W39) — the redeployment/disposal decision
- Delivery scheduling (links to VS-06 / W196) — the utilization driver

steps.activity: Calculates: % available hours delivering, % capacity utilized per trip, idle time; targets ≥75% utilization; identifies underutilized for redeployment or disposal

Automation Opportunity: - Owned-fleet emissions auto-computed from fuel data; reduction-opportunity auto-flagged
Controls: - CTL-414 (ensure controlled execution — Fleet Total Cost of Ownership Analytics (PA-61.3).)
- CTL-414 (ESG-reporting accuracy — links to VS-25); operational: VP Supply Chain annual sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **3PL-emissions-estimate-uncertainty risk**: the 3PL emissions are estimated (BuildRight doesn't have the 3PL's fuel data), introducing uncertainty; mitigated by the documented estimation methodology and the conservative assumption
- **Scope-3-boundary risk**: the boundary of "fleet emissions" is ambiguous (owned only? owned + 3PL? last-mile partner?); mitigated by the documented boundary per the GHG-protocol scope definition
System Touchpoints: - ESG/sustainability (links to VS-25 / W192 GHG emissions, VS-73 / circular economy) — the carbon-footprint reporting
- Fleet/telematics (links to VS-06 / W199, VS-61 / W2313 fuel) — the fuel data
- 3PL (links to VS-56 / W242) — the 3PL emissions estimate

steps.activity: Calculates: fuel × emission factor; estimates 3PL emissions from volume; identifies reduction: route optimization, fuel-efficient, alternative fuels, load optimization; feeds VS-25

Automation Opportunity: - Incident-cost auto-aggregated; high-risk-driver auto-flagged from telematics
Controls: - CTL-414 (ensure controlled execution — Fleet Total Cost of Ownership Analytics (PA-61.3).)
- CTL-414 (OHS/fleet-safety — links to VS-24); operational: VP Supply Chain quarterly sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Underreporting risk**: minor incidents (a backing scrape) go unreported, hiding the true safety cost; mitigated by the telematics-incident-detection (harsh-impact alert) supplementing self-report

- **Cost-vs-safety-trade-off-misframing risk**: safety investment is framed as cost rather than accident-avoidance savings; mitigated by the cost-of-accidents-avoided view alongside the safety-program cost
System Touchpoints: - Safety/incident (links to VS-24 / W140 OHS, VS-06 / W197 driver safety) — the incident data
- Cost (links to VS-61 / W2323 insurance, W2324 maintenance) — the safety-cost composite
- Telematics (links to VS-06 / W199) — the driver-behavior (harsh-braking, speeding) input
Time Estimate: ~6–9 hours/quarter (per the step durations) = **~24–36 hours/year** Safety Officer.

steps.activity: Analyzes: accident repair, cargo damage, insurance premium impact, driver injury, third-party liability; recommends: training, safety features, route risk assessment

fields.Participants: Procurement, Finance, Logistics Manager, VP Supply Chain

Controls: - CTL-414 (3PL-contract accuracy — links to VS-03); CTL-48 (rate-dispute resolution); operational: VP Supply Chain sign-off on negotiation/transition
Pain Points / Risks: - **Above-market-partner-stickiness risk**: an above-market partner is retained because transitioning is disruptive; mitigated by the documented transition-plan and the staged volume-shift
- **Benchmark-confound risk**: the market benchmark is for a different service level (a cheaper 3PL with worse SLA); mitigated by the like-for-like (same SLA, same lane) comparison
System Touchpoints: - 3PL contract (links to VS-56 / W62B onboarding, VS-03 / W62 contract, VS-61 / W2321 route benchmark) — the partner rates
- Market benchmark (links to VS-27 / W113, VS-56 / W242) — the market-rate comparison
- Transition (links to VS-56 / W62B offboarding) — the partner-transition planning

steps.activity: Benchmarks vs. market; identifies above-market partners; negotiates reductions; Finance validates savings; Logistics plans transition if needed per VS-56

Controls: - CTL-414 (ensure controlled execution — Fleet Total Cost of Ownership Analytics (PA-61.3).)
- CTL-414 (cost/revenue accuracy — links to VS-17, VS-158); operational: CFO monthly sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Benchmark-apples-to-oranges risk**: the Philippine-retail benchmark defines "logistics cost" differently than BuildRight; mitigated by the definition-mapping before comparison

- **Revenue-mix-distortion risk**: a shift to higher-revenue (lower-logistics-intensity) categories lowers the % without a real logistics improvement; mitigated by the like-for-like (same-mix) view alongside the headline
System Touchpoints: - FP&A (links to VS-17 / W26 budget, VS-158 / W85) — the logistics-cost and revenue
- Benchmark (links to VS-61 / W2321, VS-72 / W2591 shared-services benchmarking pattern) — the Philippine-retail benchmark
- COO dashboard (links to VS-28 / W231 QBR) — the KPI presentation

steps.activity: Calculates: logistics cost % of revenue and COGS; benchmarks vs. Philippine retail (8–12% of COGS); presents to COO with variance analysis

fields.Volume: ~40 owned vehicles (the owned-fleet canon) + 3PL surge capacity

Automation Opportunity: - Plan auto-assembled from the replacement/expansion/tech datasets; scenario (growth low/mid/high) auto-modeled
Controls: - CTL-414 (ensure controlled execution — Fleet Total Cost of Ownership Analytics (PA-61.3).)
- operational: capex-approval — links to VS-40; operational: CEO/Board approval of the 5-year plan
Pain Points / Risks: - **Plan-vs-actual-divergence risk**: the 5-year plan is overtaken by store-growth changes or fuel-price shifts; mitigated by the annual refresh (not a one-time 5-year lock)

- **Over-investment risk**: the plan over-provisions fleet for a growth that doesn't materialize, leaving idle capacity; mitigated by the elastic-capacity preference (3PL surge) over permanent fleet expansion where feasible
System Touchpoints: - Capex plan (links to VS-40 / W21 capex, VS-112 PMO) — the 5-year investment plan
- Fleet/asset (links to VS-04 / W52, VS-35 / W39, VS-61 / W2326 TCO) — the replacement/expansion inputs
- Tech/telematics (links to VS-27 / W366, VS-61 / W2315 alternative-fuel) — the technology investments
Time Estimate: ~7 days/year = **~50–60 hours/year** VP Supply Chain + CFO.

steps.activity: Develops: replacement schedule, expansion for store growth (10–15/year), technology (GPS, telematics, EV charging); CEO/Board approve; feeds VS-40 Capex budget
